title: Wild Gorillas Sing While They Eat, and the Silverback Sings the Most

scenes.text: Gorillas sing at dinner. The silverback sings the most.
Scientists followed two groups of wild western lowland gorillas through the forests of the Republic of Congo.
As the gorillas chewed, they hummed and sang. Low, rumbling sounds that only came out at mealtimes.
Water plants, flowers and seeds got the most singing. The foods gorillas prize.
Adult males sang the most. Females and youngsters stayed quiet, maybe to avoid drawing predators.
The silverback is the one who decides when a meal ends. The song may be his way of saying: not yet. Pass the flowers.

description:
Wild western lowland gorillas hum and sing while they feed, a 2016 study in PLOS ONE found after following two groups in the Republic of Congo.
Aquatic plants, flowers and seeds triggered the most calls; adult males, including the dominant silverbacks, called far more than females and juveniles. The researchers suggest the calls express well-being and help coordinate the group, with the silverback possibly signalling when it is time to move on.
Which animal sound would you most like to understand?
subject: silverback gorilla
first_comment: The study followed just 20 gorillas, and the scientists could not yet tell whether the humming and the singing mean different things. What do you think a gorilla is saying?
